topic: Q1: Provisions of Partnership Act in Absence of Deed
question: Practical Problem 1: X, Y and Z are partners without a Partnership Deed. Capital contributions: X ₹50,000, Y ₹40,000, Z ₹20,000. X claims 10% interest on capital; Y demands ₹1,000/month salary; Z claims 10% interest on partner loan of ₹25,000. Net profit for the year is ₹60,000. Settle disputes as per the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
solution_steps: In the absence of a Partnership Deed, Section 13 applies:
• Interest on Capital: NOT ALLOWED to any partner.
• Interest on Partner Loan: Strictly allowed @ 6% p.a. (Z receives ₹1,500).
• Divisible Profit of ₹58,500 shared EQUALLY (1:1:1) = ₹19,500 each.
working_notes: Section 13 mandates equal profit distribution irrespective of capital contributed.
